subject: Early-token latency blips affecting Hosted API — upstream TLS/CDN investigation
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@bluewave-analytics.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes in Hosted API (first-token latency)

Rachel —

We started seeing a noticeable increase in TTFT for our calls to your hosted endpoint around 07:30 PDT. P95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.1s and p99 is spiking above 2.4s. This started right after your team rolled the CDN TLS cert rotation (we were told). It’s causing timeouts in our real-time feature pipeline and we’re seeing ~3% errors per minute from downstream processors.

Attached is a short trace from our side showing the initial TLS handshake delays and a few failing requests. Can you confirm if this is on your side or if you can provide a mitigation? Our sprint release is blocked.

Thanks,
Jordan Hayes
Director, Platform Engineering
BlueWave Analytics

Attachments: bw-ttft-trace-20260709.json (trace), screenshot-err-07-34.png (image)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 spikes in Hosted API (first-token latency)

Investigation notes (quick):
- Observed elevated TTFT in US-WEST region beginning ~07:28 PDT.
- Correlated with our CDN provider’s cert roll (log window 07:20–07:35) and a sharp rise in TCP/TLS handshake times on edges serving us-west POPs.
- p95 TTFT climbed from ~210ms to ~1.05s; p99 up to ~2.5s for short-lived connections.
- Long-lived keepalive connections did not show the same magnitude of regression.

Action taken:
- Rolled a short config to favor persistent connections for high-QPS customers while we work w/ CDN.
- Captured PCAP from edge and attached (cdn-handshake-20260709.pcap).
- Opening a live bridge with CDN ops.

Next: validate rollback of cert-change or request them to re-prime TLS session cache on involved edges. I’ll follow up with trace comparisons (attached trace from BlueWave vs our server-side tracing).

— Laura Bennett
SRE Lead, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cdn-handshake-20260709.pcap, server-trace-07-09.log

If we can get BlueWave back to baseline with the persistent-connection temp config + CDN re-prime, that’s preferable before escalating. If not contained in 90 mins, escalate to vendor SLT and loop in VP Ops.

Also, Monica — please prepare a short one-paragraph exec note for our CRO/CEO with impact (customers affected, p95/p99 delta, mitigation steps) so that we can proactively brief leadership.

— Markus Klein
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@bluewave-analytics.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 spikes in Hosted API (first-token latency)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the rapid heads-up and for the trace. Quick summary of what we found and immediate steps: 
- Root cause: transient upstream TLS handshake delays at CDN edges serving us-west after a certificate rotation window; this increased TTFT for short-lived connections and caused p95/p99 regressions.
- Mitigation applied: we temporarily favored persistent connections for your traffic and asked the CDN to re-prime session caches on affected edges — we see p95 trending back toward baseline (~230ms) in our telemetry.
- Next steps: our SRE will continue monitoring for 4 hours and provide a post-incident note with full traces and timelines. We’re also coordinating a follow-up with the CDN to avoid similar regressions during cert rotations (we will ask for a staged rotation or extra priming).

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacted your real-time pipeline. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute postmortem with our SRE and CDN ops to review traces and prevention steps.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192
